holidays.name: National Caviar Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in fish roe, from fancy sturgeon caviar to budget-friendly alternatives. Fancy crackers and tiny spoons are encouraged, and pinkies may be raised.
holidays.origin: Like many American food days, it appeared through food-industry promotion and internet calendars, with no single documented founder.
holidays.funFact: Some of the world's rarest caviar, from albino sturgeon, has sold for tens of thousands of dollars per kilogram.

holidays.name: World Listening Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to paying attention to the sounds around us, from birdsong to traffic hum. Participants take sound walks and appreciate the acoustic environment.
holidays.origin: Started in 2010 by the World Listening Project, and the date honors the birthday of R. Murray Schafer, the Canadian composer who founded the study of acoustic ecology.
holidays.funFact: Schafer coined the term 'soundscape' and wrote about how modern noise pollution is changing the way humanity hears the world.

holidays.name: Get to Know Your Customers Day
holidays.description: A day when businesses are encouraged to step out from behind the counter and actually talk to the people who pay them, ideally without a survey popup.
holidays.origin: Created by business and customer-service circles and observed on the third Thursday of July, so it can fall on or near July 18 depending on the year.
holidays.funFact: Studies often cite that retaining an existing customer costs far less than acquiring a new one, which is the whole point of this day.

holidays.name: Nelson Mandela International Day
holidays.description: A global day of service where people are asked to spend 67 minutes helping others or improving their communities, not a quirky party but a meaningful observance.
holidays.origin: The United Nations declared it in 2009, first observed in 2010, honoring Mandela's birthday on July 18, 1918.
holidays.funFact: The 67 minutes represent the 67 years Mandela spent fighting for human rights and social justice.

holidays.name: Hot Dog Day Adjacent: Play Ball Pitching Anniversary Vibes
holidays.description: Not official, but fans mark the day by celebrating baseball's oddities such as the Pine Tar Game, which was replayed after a ruling that overturned a home run over sticky bat residue.
holidays.origin: The famous Pine Tar Incident happened on July 24, 1983, so this is a bit of a stretch for July 18, but baseball fans love trivia days in mid-July.
holidays.funFact: The league ruled the pine tar on George Brett's bat was legal after all, and the game was finished weeks later with only a few minutes of play.
